cells.tense: You are still carrying it, and the weight has settled into a steadiness you no longer have to talk about.
cells.act: stand firm in the material hardship
cells.ask: Take the heaviest thing you're holding that no one else can hold for you, and stand firm in it — don't hand off a part, don't mention it to anyone. Keep standing, without a clock on it.
cells.core:
You can tell what deserves your attention before you can explain why. It's the sense that lets you put a thing down and pick up another without a meeting about it. When your attention is steady, persistence is what you do with it — not from a stock of answers, but from a hope that's been rained on and is still up. There's no name for it. It's just what you do on a Wednesday. What you attend to holds because you don't flinch from it.

Steadfastness, when it's well, holds without forcing. It takes the weight and doesn't crush what's underneath. Give it a floor. Choose the heaviest thing you're already carrying that nobody else can take from you, and stand firm in it without asking anyone to shoulder a piece. Not to prove anything. You'll find out what your reserves feel like when nothing is propped against them, and what matters to you will stand out clearer for it.
cells.sheetLine: What you attend to holds because you stay with it.
cells.place: in a place of knowing what to attend to

cells.tense: You are getting ready for the next stretch of weight before this one has told you what it is.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Hold both things that are true about the situation you keep turning over. No announcement, no verdict, no plan. Keep them level and leave no end date on it.
cells.core:
You've been lasting — that part is real — and somewhere in it the planning got out in front of the living. What's going well doesn't get to stay well for an hour before the next load is measured, the next version braced for. Persistence under that kind of management stops being strength and becomes a way to avoid finding out what's coming; the load gets heavier because you won't set it down.

There's a plainer knowing underneath all of it — the one that doesn't argue, that saw the shape of things before you built a plan around them. Give it the week. Take whatever you're already managing, hold both of the true things about it, and don't declare either one. Let the answer stay pending. What you're attending to will still be there when you finally say what you actually think, and you'll be saying it from having been with it the whole time.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing for a weight the situation hasn't handed you yet.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door you already walked through, wondering if it was the right one.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Tend something near you that's gone a while without care. Give it exactly what it needs, and once you've done that, stop. Nothing beyond what it actually needs.
cells.core:
Nothing tells you what matters the way it usually does. Your attention has gone back over old ground, and while it's there it isn't here, so the things that need you get whatever's left. Old questions keep getting reopened and nothing new gets taken up. That isn't care failing. It's what an empty hand does — it clutches what it already knows.

The way out isn't by pushing harder at your attention. It's by looking after something with a steady hand — care that doesn't exhaust you and doesn't hold on too tight. Take one thing near you, give it exactly what it needs, then leave it be. You'll find out that what you attend to doesn't need to be defended in order to grow, and your sense of what matters returns with the work, not before it.
cells.sheetLine: You know what matters. You've stopped turning toward it.

cells.tense: You are still carrying it, and you've been calling the carrying just what's happening.
cells.act: keep going without checking on anyone else
cells.ask: Next time something presses on you, keep going through it one beat longer before you hand anything off or ask how it landed. No plan, no announcement. Just stay in it one beat.
cells.core:
You keep going, and it isn't circumstance. It's your own weight holding the line, and your account of it says you had no choice. The thing that contains the pressure without crushing anyone under it is doing what it does, and your name isn't on it. You talk about your persistence as something that happens to you.

Go back to the plain fact: some pressure is on you right now, and your own strength is holding it. When something small presses on you this week, don't move through it fast and don't pass it along. Stay in it one beat longer before you hand anything off or ask how it landed. Not to last forever — just to notice that the standing is yours. What you give people is you shouldering it, and you deserve to know it's you.
cells.sheetLine: What holds the line is you, not the day.
